16.3. An XML Parser That Accepts a DOCTYPE Reads Files for the Sender

gates.says: all 5 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-length-header: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-header: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-header: 16.1 runs ASCIIChannel with XMLPackager and shows 0197 followed by the <isomsg> XML, and says XML behind a length header needs only a different pair in the channel configuration, with no new code.
recorded.prompt:q-json-timeout: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-json-timeout: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-json-timeout: 16.1 says an unanswered JSON 0200 has an unknown outcome, that dropping the reversal queue leads to a resend or a forgotten purchase, and that reversals depend on the messages, not the syntax. The page implies a reversal is right but never says 'reverse on timeout'; that rule comes from unit 4.
recorded.prompt:q-xml-entity: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-xml-entity: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-xml-entity: 16.3's run shows XML2003Packager putting the file's content into field 48, and the text says a server that answers echoes by cloning the request sends field 48 back to the sender.
recorded.prompt:q-card-link: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-card-link: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-card-link: 16.4 says card authorization between acquirers, networks and issuers is still overwhelmingly ISO 8583, and the 16.6 summary says it stays on ISO 8583 for now.
recorded.prompt:q-merchant-name: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-merchant-name: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-merchant-name: 16.5 says the packager refuses an over-long field 43, that someone has to decide what to cut and how the network wants it laid out in 40 characters, and that the mapping is written field by field with the other party.

gates.says: all 15 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-length-header:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-header:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-header:b: 16.1's XMLChannel output has no length prefix, the text says it reads lines until the closing </isomsg>, and the 16.7 table says 'no length header'.
recorded.prompt:q-length-header:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-header:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-header:c: 16.1 says the packager makes the bytes and the channel only frames them, and that a partner who wants XML behind a length header 'needs no new code'.
recorded.prompt:q-length-header:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-length-header:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-length-header:d: 16.1 says ASCIIChannel puts a length 'in front of whatever the packager produced, XML included', and the run shows 0197 before the XML.
recorded.prompt:q-json-timeout:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-json-timeout:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-json-timeout:a: 16.1 names this exact belief (the API 'answers every request') and says resending on a timeout can make the cardholder pay twice.
recorded.prompt:q-json-timeout:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-json-timeout:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-json-timeout:b: 16.1 says resending makes the cardholder pay twice, and the 16.2 JSON example carries field 11 ("11": 417), so JSON does carry a STAN.
recorded.prompt:q-json-timeout:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-json-timeout:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-json-timeout:d: 16.1 says an unanswered request has an unknown outcome and that forgetting it leaves the cardholder paying for a sale the merchant reported as failed. Partly true: its premise, that the partner could have declined it, is correct; only the conclusion is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-xml-entity:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-xml-entity:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-xml-entity:a: 16.3 says only XMLPackager refuses a DOCTYPE and XML2003Packager turns that check off in its constructor. Partly true: it holds for XMLPackager, but the option says it of all jPOS packagers.
recorded.prompt:q-xml-entity:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-xml-entity:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-xml-entity:b: 16.3 says message text is input from another system 'even on an authenticated link', and the run shows XML2003Packager accepting the DOCTYPE.
recorded.prompt:q-xml-entity:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-xml-entity:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-xml-entity:d: 16.3's run shows field 48 = zmk.component=..., the file's content rather than its name or the entity reference.
recorded.prompt:q-card-link:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-card-link:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-card-link:a: 16.4 ties the move off SWIFT MT to cross-border payments between banks and says card authorization is still overwhelmingly ISO 8583; 16.9 explains why card networks stay on it. The page refutes 'soon' only as a statement of where things stand now, since 16.4 also says 'this changes faster than course material'.
recorded.prompt:q-card-link:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-card-link:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-card-link:b: 16.4 says that although ISO 20022 defines card messages, card authorization still runs on ISO 8583. Partly true: the premise that ISO 20022 defines acquirer-to-issuer card messages is stated on the page.
recorded.prompt:q-card-link:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-card-link:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-card-link:d: 16.4 says ISO 20022 'also defines card messages, from the acceptor to the acquirer and from the acquirer to the issuer'.
recorded.prompt:q-merchant-name:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-merchant-name:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-merchant-name:a: 16.5 shows 'pack: error packing field 43' and says the packager refuses the message on the first merchant with a long name. The run uses 51 characters, not the stem's 47, but the page's statement is general.
recorded.prompt:q-merchant-name:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-merchant-name:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-merchant-name:b: 16.5 shows the packager refusing a value that is too long, so it does not cut. Partly true: 16.2 says the 1987 packager does pad, numeric fields with zeros and alphanumeric fields with spaces, so only the 'cut' half is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-merchant-name:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-merchant-name:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-merchant-name:d: 16.5 says field 43 has 40 characters 'for the name and location', which contradicts the reason given; the page never discusses private fields for this case.

gates.says: each of the 5 questions keys exactly 1 of its distinct options and every option carries the sentence its reader is shown
each of the 5 questions cites a passage the ledger still digests to the value this exercise was built from
